A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 19-page versions of NLPrompt, including Appendices A–E. Corresponding text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, noisy-label comparisons, ablations and supplementary analyses in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix experiments, with one revised performance entry.

M1.justification: PromptOT purification, dataset partitioning and the combined CE/MAE training procedure remain unchanged. Changing the pseudo-label symbol from tilde-y to hat-y in Section 5 is a notation correction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight synthetic-noise datasets, including SUN397 in Appendix C.1, and Food101N. The represented tasks and noise scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments, including CoOp, GCE and JoAPR; VPT, MaPLe and PromptSRC; and the supplementary CLIP-ZS and Mixup comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported noise-generation procedures, train/test splits, shot counts, model backbones, training budgets and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Section 6 and Appendix C.

E4.justification: The few-shot analysis, component ablations, purification comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity experiments, JoAPR-setting comparison and computational-overhead study are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three runs with different seeds in Section 6.3. Table A8's uncertainty reporting and the figures' shaded bands are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises NLPrompt's EuroSAT accuracy at 62.5% asymmetric noise from 66.33% to 37.27% under unchanged reported settings. It still exceeds JoAPR's 33.93%, so the ranking is preserved. Although substantial for this setting, the revision affects only one performance entry.

T1.justification: Appendix E revises Equation (48) in the proof of Theorem E.4, replacing several intermediate bounds with a direct comparison of updated coefficient ratios. A new sentence invokes the ordering of current ratios and increment ratios. The theorem, assumptions and remaining derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about PromptMAE's robustness, PromptOT's purification role and NLPrompt's performance. The main theoretical guarantee is unchanged.

C2.justification: The scientific interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including Appendix D's explanation of weaker performance at low noise levels and the conclusion's proposed extension to imbalanced distributions.

D1.justification: The implementation settings, optimizer, hardware, timing information and code-repository link are unchanged. No additional reproducibility information is disclosed.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prompt learning, noisy-label learning and feature learning theory remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the pseudo-label notation in Section 5, an explanatory sentence accompanying Equation (48), and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. Section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 removes printed page-number footers and locally reformats the shortened Equation (48) and following text. All figures, table structures, captions and their placements are retained.

improvement.justification: The Section 5 notation correction improves local clarity, but the substantive revisions have an uncertain quality benefit. Table 1's EuroSAT change from 66.33% to 37.27% is unexplained. Equation (48) removes problematic intermediate bounds, but ordering current ratios and increment ratios does not generally establish the claimed ordering after adding the increments. Thus the PDFs do not establish a reliable net improvement in empirical reliability or theoretical rigor.
